Simulate Correlated Samples from Triangular Distributions

Source: R/property-simulation.R
simulate_correlated_triangular.Rd

Generates n correlated samples from length(params) triangular distributions via a Cholesky decomposition of correlation_matrix applied to standard-normal draws, then transforms each column to its own triangular distribution via the inverse CDF.

Usage

simulate_correlated_triangular(
  n,
  params,
  correlation_matrix,
  random_seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Integer, number of samples to generate.

params

List of c(a, b, c) triples, one per distribution - note the order here is (lower, mode, upper), unlike tri_dist()'s own (a = lower, b = upper, c = mode) convention. Preserved exactly as the legacy source defines it; a real source of confusion if assumed to match tri_dist()'s argument order.

correlation_matrix

A square, positive-semi-definite correlation matrix, length(params) x length(params).

random_seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility.

Value

A matrix of correlated samples, n rows x length(params) columns.
